EV-GPS-00213 is MISSING — weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; the driver device never uploaded a trace and the platform holds no object at all under this trip_id. There is therefore no qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the trip. Limb (b) is not made out, and on POL-NS-02's own words a trace containing no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes before cancellation means the driver never arrived and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee. The absence of the trace is itself citable evidence.

Limb (c) does not measure dwell from the driver's recollection or from his arrival tap: the clause runs the clock from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and requires a continuous dwell of at least the free waiting period in force. With no trace there is no qualifying fix, so no dwell start and no dwell length can be established, and the driver's counter-statement ('from about 5.47 to 5.53') is a party statement that cannot supply the clock the clause demands. The trip_record arrived_at of 17:47:05 is a driver-pressed BUTTON marker (trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is BUTTON), and POL-NS-12 covers only a GPS_AUTO platform arrival event, so that tap cannot stand in for limb (b) or limb (c).

Because this is a BUTTON arrival, POL-NS-05 is the clause that polices it, and limb (ii) says that where no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip the cancellation fee is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the trip is recorded as a false-arrival event in the ruling's referrals. That is exactly the state of this record: EV-GPS-00213 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, and the marker at 17:47:05 is unverifiable rather than verified.

The rider's account that she was at the bay and messaged the driver three times cannot be run through POL-NS-04, because EV-CHAT-00213 is MISSING — weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so limbs (a) and (b) of that clause cannot be executed and the clause cannot exonerate her. The loss of the log must not, however, be read against her: trip_record.chat_message_count is 3, so the platform's own telemetry proves a chat log existed for this trip and has not been produced, and POL-NS-08(c) makes a chat log holding fewer messages than chat_message_count records an impaired artifact. POL-NS-06 requires the effective in-geofence dwell to be computed under POL-NS-02 and corrected under POL-NS-05 before any fee is chargeable, and its limb (i) lets dwell be accumulated across separate intervals only where a traffic_advisory actually covers the pickup road and carries a qualifying type. EV-ADVIS-00213-01 is MISSING — weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; no advisory covers the Jurong East interchange in this window. Limb (i) is therefore unavailable to the driver, he cannot be credited with accumulated dwell on any view, and the dwell computation cannot be performed at all on this record.

The free waiting period in force for this trip is the 300 seconds recorded in trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, read under POL-NS-01(c), and POL-NS-06 refunds the fee in full where the effective dwell is shorter than it. The deciding fact — whether the driver was inside the geofence and for how long — is carried only by the gps_trace, and that artifact's weight_multiplier is 0.0. POL-NS-09(c) is engaged on the face of the profiles: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 2 — the same rider and this same driver, twice in the trailing 90 days, which the rider's own claim text ('Same driver as the last two times') matches. Both fields are citable for this test under POL-GEN-01. claims.text: The trip record for this trip is COMPLETE and admissible at weight 1.0, and on its face it records the driver's 'arrived' event at 17:47:05 and the driver's termination of the trip at 17:53:40 - an interval of 395 seconds, matching the record's own wait_time_min of 6.6. That exceeds the free waiting period in force for this trip, which POL-NS-01(c) reads from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec (300 seconds for this TRANSPORT_HUB pickup), not the 180-second default. The consideration the $6.00 fee is meant to buy was given.

Limb (d) of POL-NS-01 is satisfied on the face of the same complete record. The trip_record shows no boarding event, shows the trip terminated by the DRIVER, and carries cancellation_reason_code RIDER_UNREACHABLE - one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) expressly recognises, alongside RIDER_NO_SHOW and EXCESSIVE_WAIT. Nothing in the record is a DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE admission by the driver.

The driver's GPS trace is gone: EV-GPS-00213 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0, and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT. I disclose that plainly and do not present it as clean. But a MISSING artifact carries no fact, and POL-NS-02's own proviso treats a trace too sparse to yield three consecutive in-radius readings as impaired evidence rather than proof of absence; POL-GEN-02 says the same of an artifact at weight 0.0. The rider cannot convert a failed device upload into an affirmative finding that the driver never reached the bay, and no admissible artifact places the driver outside the 150 m TRANSPORT_HUB arrival radius.

The rider's case rides on POL-NS-04, and that clause cannot be run. Limb (a) requires the chat_log to show a message from the rider whose content is locating or coordinating; limb (b) requires the chat_log to show the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor made an in-app call. EV-CHAT-00213 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so neither limb can be established, and the authorship, content and timing of the three messages recorded by trip_record.chat_message_count are simply unknown. POL-NS-04 therefore cannot exonerate the rider, and the driver's account that he answered every message is left unrebutted.

Those two fields are citable under POL-GEN-01 for exactly this test, and POL-NS-09(c) makes 2 or more same-pair no-show disputes in the trailing 90 days a mandatory escalation. On this record the fee must not be returned to the rider.

The fare line is not defective, and no refund follows from the arithmetic. trip_record.platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd is $6.00, and the $6.00 cancellation_fee in the fare breakdown is the greater of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone fee ($6.00) and the RYDE_X tier fee ($4.00), so the charged line reconciles with the fee in force under the resolution rule and POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. The payment record supports the fee rather than undermining it.

I flag that this entitlement depends on the arrival finding, and that the artifact which would put it beyond argument is the missing EV-GPS-00213 at weight 0.0 (MISSING_ARTIFACT); the $4.80 figure itself is read from the money block, not asserted.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this case goes to a human reviewer. The disputed $6.00 cancellation fee stays on hold — neither collected from you nor refunded — until that review is decided. That is already the state of the fare record, whose payment_status is PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

WHY IT ESCALATES. POL-NS-09(c) makes escalation mandatory where the same rider and the same driver have 2 or more no-show disputes in the trailing 90 days. Both profiles carry that figure: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 2 (EV-RPROF-00213 and EV-DPROF-00213, each weight 1.0), which matches the rider's own words, 'same driver as the last two times'. Escalation is TERMINAL: it replaces any monetary ruling, so I issue no refund and no compensation. Both advocates agree this trigger is engaged.

WHY THE FEE ITSELF CANNOT BE DECIDED HERE. The two instruments that would decide it are absent. The driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00213, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and the chat log (EV-CHAT-00213, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) are not in the platform's pipeline. Those are the artifacts that settle whether the driver was inside the 150 m TRANSPORT_HUB arrival radius (POL-NS-02) and whether he held the free waiting period measured from GPS entry (POL-NS-01(c)). Without them those limbs are UNDECIDED — not failed, and not satisfied.

DRIVER'S POINTS. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00213, weight 1.0) is complete and does show an 'arrived' event at 17:47:05 and a driver cancellation at 17:53:40, a 395-second interval, with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_UNREACHABLE — one of the codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, so limb (d) is met. But POL-NS-01(c) runs the dwell clock from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap, and trip_record.platform_policy.arrival_marker is BUTTON, so POL-NS-12's platform-confirmed (GPS_AUTO) shortcut is unavailable. The 395 seconds therefore cannot establish the required 300-second free-wait dwell, and the $4.80 payout the money block computes at 80% of $6.00 is not reached. The anti-farming check does NOT trip — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 3, below the count of 4, and 3 of 107 completed trips is 2.8%, below the 8% rate — so no compensation is withheld on that ground and no refund is directed into any packet. The claim mentioning prior_no_show_flags is noted only to record that that lifetime counter is NOT the field POL-NS-07 reads; it was used for nothing.

RIDER'S POINTS. A missing trace is not a trace showing the driver outside the radius: POL-NS-02's proviso addresses a sparse trace, whereas a missing artifact carries no fact at all, so limb (b) is undecided rather than failed and no full refund follows. POL-NS-05's false-arrival referral is likewise not established, because testing whether the 17:47:05 button tap was false needs a GPS fix and there is none; that question stays open for the reviewer and is not a clause-mandated referral. POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider because its limbs (a) and (b) both read the chat log, which is absent — but the loss is not held against her: trip_record.chat_message_count of 3 shows a log existed, making the chat log impaired under POL-NS-08(c), and the driver's assertion that he answered every message is equally unverifiable. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00213-01, weight 0.0) removes POL-NS-06 limb (i)'s dwell accumulation from the driver's side as well.

WHAT I ACCEPT. The fare line reconciles: the $6.00 cancellation_fee equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged and no refund follows from the arithmetic.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR THE REVIEWER. (1) Was the driver inside the 150 m arrival radius, and did he hold 300 seconds measured from GPS entry (POL-NS-02, POL-NS-01(c))? (2) Did he reply within 120 seconds, or make an in-app call (POL-NS-04(b))? (3) Was the BUTTON arrival marker false (POL-NS-05)? These cannot be answered on the present record, which is why the fee is held rather than decided.

At 2 or more such disputes escalation is mandatory: no monetary outcome issues, the disputed fee is placed on hold rather than collected or refunded, and the rider is not left carrying the disputed charge while the reviewer settles the open question of the driver's arrival.
